decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach to the left tube, raising the wrist and gradually pitching the open gripper downward.
Advance above the left tube while completing the downward grasp orientation; maintain elbow-up continuity.
Center the open fingers over the upper body of the left tube and descend to grasp height.
Make a small wrist-view centering correction and close around the first tube.
Lift the closed grasp clear of the table and retract slightly before turning the tube upright.
The tube remains between the fingers. Turn it toward upright while moving toward the left rack slots.
Finish making the first tube upright and approach the left-front large opening at clearance height.
Use smaller rotation increments after the continuity guard; establish upright alignment and lower toward the rack.
Lower the upright tube toward the left-front opening with a small forward centering correction; keep the grasp closed.
Insert the first tube the remaining short distance into the aligned opening, pausing closed to inspect seating.
The tube shifted relative to the fingers near the opening. Lift slightly, recenter toward the visible hole, and retry gently rather than pushing.
Release the tube at the opening and withdraw the open fingers, checking whether it settles upright independently.
Withdraw the left arm from the released tube and start an elbow-up right-arm approach to the nearer-right tube.
Continue the right gripper toward the inner-right tube, rotating to its table-plane direction; ease the empty left arm toward home.
Finish the downward orientation and descend above the inner-right tube, leaving the fingers open for visual centering.
Shift the right grasp toward the tube's upper body using the wrist view, then close without dragging along the table.
Lift the second tube clear with the right gripper closed before rotating toward the rack.
Rotate the retained second tube gradually toward upright while carrying it inward above the right rack openings.
Continue the slow upright rotation and inward carry with the second tube retained in the right gripper.
Complete upright orientation and center the second tube above the right-front large rack opening.
Correct the right tube laterally over the outer large opening while descending slowly to inspect the entry alignment.
Make a small right/back centering correction and lower the second tube gently into the outer opening.
The second tube is at the opening with contact. Open and retreat rather than force it, allowing it to settle independently.
The second tube toppled instead of seating. Clear the open right gripper and inspect its resting position for recovery.
Keep clear while the dislodged tube settles, then reassess its pickup orientation.
Approach the unobstructed remaining tabletop tube with an open downward grasp; leave the fallen tube undisturbed for recovery.
Continue pitching the right gripper downward while approaching the unobstructed tabletop tube.
Finish matching the tabletop tube's direction and descend with open fingers to inspect grasp centering.
Refine the tube-axis and lateral centering from the wrist view, then close around its upper body.
Lift the grasped tabletop tube clear before assessing and correcting its upright alignment.
Turn the retained tube toward upright while carrying it inward, keeping clearance above the rack.
Continue the smooth upright rotation and inward carry, retaining the tube above rack height.
Finish the upright rotation and position above the right-side opening, pausing above contact for visual alignment.
Use a smaller descent for the differently positioned grasp, correcting slightly forward over the right opening before deeper insertion.
Keep lateral alignment fixed and lower gently, watching for tube motion relative to the fingers or rack.
The tube rose in the fingers at contact. Lift slightly and shift toward the visible neighboring opening rather than pushing down.
Test the corrected opening with a very small straight descent, maintaining the closed grasp and checking seating before release.
The tube now moves with the gripper at the corrected opening; lower the final short distance to seating depth.
Open in place at seating depth, pause for the tube to settle, then withdraw the right fingers without lifting the tube.
The right tube stands independently. Clear the right arm and begin an elbow-up left approach to recover the fallen tube in front of the rack.
Approach the fallen tube with the left arm, gradually turning the downward gripper to match its reversed cap direction; return the right arm home.
Replan after the wrist-joint continuity guard with smaller rotations and the shorter safe wrist-turn direction for the reversed tube.
Ease the right arm through its near-home configuration and continue the left downward approach with gradual wrist rotation toward the reversed tube.
Continue the slow downward-wrist turn above the reversed tube, staying on the left side of the workspace.
Complete the gradual wrist turn to put the fallen tube's cap along the grasp axis, then approach its body with open fingers.
Fine-align the reversed tube in the wrist image and descend the open fingers to its body without touching the rack.
Center the reversed tube between the left fingers and close in place for recovery.
Lift the recovered tube and retract leftward away from the rack before unwinding the wrist to turn it upright.
Begin a slow wrist-unwinding rotation of the recovered reversed tube toward upright, maintaining clearance and the closed grasp.
Continue the controlled unwinding turn with the tube retained, moving toward the central rack opening while staying above it.
Continue unwinding the retained tube toward upright, with a slow approach above the center slot.
